findings.claim: Silent contradiction on the concurrent-exclusive race: 11.01.05 says the losing buyer is QUEUED behind the hold, while 11.02.01 D-12, 11.08.02 and the 11.01 CX file all say the second attempt is REFUSED and explicitly not queued. Neither statement carries a marker, and 11.01.05 does not cite D-12.

findings.failureScenario: Buyer A and Buyer B both request an exclusive sync licence for work W at overlapping scope. An implementer specifying from 11.01.05 builds a durable request queue: B's request persists and auto-activates when A's hold lapses. An implementer specifying from 11.02.01 D-12 builds a hard refusal plus an optional lapse notification, with no persisted request. The two products differ in whether B holds anything after the refusal, whether B is charged or committed on auto-activation, and whether the platform can end up auto-issuing an exclusive to B without a fresh gate re-check — which D-04 forbids. Because 11.01.05 does not cite D-12, the divergence is not self-correcting on a per-file read.

findings.claim: 11.02.02 D-12 requires the gate to block new issuance for a work under a verified non-listed authorship claim WITHOUT invalidating the attestation, and specifies a buyer-facing 'Contested' state — but 11.02.01's verdict enum is closed and contains no value that can express it. Every candidate value is false by its own definition.

Fail closed (11.02.02 CX-01 Q5 — the addition always wins).'
findings.failureScenario: A verified non-listed claimant asserts a writer share in work W. Under 11.02.02 D-12 the existing attestation stays valid and the gate must refuse new issuance. Implementer A maps this to `incomplete` — but `incomplete` is defined as 'no valid completeness attestation exists', which is untrue here, and D-09 routes `incomplete` to remedy owner 11.02.02 ('[Attest]'), sending the owner to re-attest a valid attestation. Implementer B maps it to `blocked` — but `blocked` is defined as a policy/veto refusal and is declared terminal with no remedy owner, so the work never returns to the pool when the dispute resolves. Implementer C invents a seventh enum value plus a precedence position and a remedy owner, which nothing in the tree specifies. All three render different buyer copy, and only C can produce 11.02.02's own required string 'Contested — an authorship claim is open on this work'. No open question in either file covers the verdict representation.

findings.failureScenario: Producer P requests programmatic clearance of a 4-bar sample from work W on the source owner's standing terms of '5% writer share, no fee'. Implementer A treats the deal value as £0 (no money changes hands at issue): every rev-share request passes every owner's ceiling regardless of size, and D-06's trailing 90-day window accumulates nothing, so an owner who set 'auto-approve up to £500 of my share' has in fact auto-approved unlimited perpetual equity in unlimited derivative works — the salami-slicing exposure D-06 exists to close, reopened through the consideration type. Implementer B treats the share value as unknown and applies D-17's fail-closed rule: every rev-share request falls through to a human, which deletes 11.05.02's entire premise ('clears a sample in seconds ... nobody asked and nothing negotiated') for the terms 11.05.02 D-03 designates as the default. The tree specifies neither, and no tracked question asks it.

findings.failureScenario: Work W holds a live non-exclusive podcast licence issued three months ago. Buyer B searches for an exclusive podcast scope. 11.02.01's verdict evaluates the consent graph, attestation, encumbrance set and effective policy — none of which sees the existing non-exclusive — and returns `clearable-now`, badged and rankable in search per D-16. B builds a pitch, negotiates, agrees terms, and is refused only at 11.08.02 precondition 4. Unlike 11.02.01 D-16's designed staleness case, this condition was knowable and static from the first query, so the search verdict is not merely stale — it is wrong. An implementer building the verdict from 11.02.01 alone omits the check entirely and issues the contradictory exclusive.

findings.failureScenario: An implementer building 11.09's compulsory-mechanical flow reaches a declared cover that is in fact a parody. The row says the platform should not adjudicate but does not say what the system does: file the statutory notice anyway (treating parody as an ordinary cover and asserting a licence the parodist may not need or may not be entitled to), refuse the flow, or surface a warning and continue. Nobody owns choosing, because the marker names no owner and no stage. The same shape holds for 11.11's staged-concert boundary, which decides whether a grand-rights licence is required at all — though its impact is bounded by 11.11 being banded WONT as a product.
